articles.title: 'SIR explain’: Smriti Irani turns Amitabh Bachchan movie scene into Rahul Gandhi jibe
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP general secretary Smriti Irani has taken a dig at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, using an AI-generated video featuring characters played by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP general secretary Smriti Irani has taken a dig at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, using an AI-generated video featuring characters played by Rahul and actor Amitabh Bachchan to target him over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The video comes amid Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders’ protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over the SIR exercise.Sharing the video on X, Irani wrote: “You can wake someone who is genuinely asleep, but not someone acting blind just to mislead the nation!”The AI-generated clip recreates a scene from Big B's film, in which Amitabh Bachchan’s character explains that his name was not deleted from the voter list because a corrupt official had not issued his death certificate. As a result, a political party used his vote and cast it in Madgaon.Irani titled the video “SIR explain”, turning it into a direct jibe at Rahul Gandhi, her former rival in the Amethi Lok Sabha constituency.Rahul has recently intensified his protests against the SIR exercise, including leading a march to the Supreme Court. articles.title: 3 arrests within 24 hours, 500-page chargesheet, 88-day probe, 3 life terms: Inside the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder case
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand Police arrested all three accused in the 2022 murder of Ankita Bhandari within 24 hours of the incident coming to light, completed
articles.body: DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand Police arrested all three accused in the 2022 murder of Ankita Bhandari within 24 hours of the incident coming to light, completed the investigation in 88 days and filed a chargesheet of around 500 pages, Additional Director General of Police (Crime and Law & Order) Dr V Murugesan said on Thursday.Addressing a press conference at Police Headquarters in Dehradun, Murugesan outlined the investigation and judicial proceedings in the case involving Bhandari, who worked at Vanantara Resort near Rishikesh.He said a Special Investigation Team (SIT) was constituted immediately on the directions of chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, given the seriousness and sensitivity of the case. A woman IPS officer of DIG rank was appointed to head the team.The SIT collected digital, technical, forensic and physical evidence during the investigation. It also examined the accused, forensic reports and witness statements, Murugesan said.The chargesheet was submitted to the court after the SIT completed its investigation within 88 days, he added.The case subsequently went to trial, with the prosecution presenting evidence collected by the SIT.On May 30, 2025, the Additional District and Sessions Court in Kotdwar convicted all three accused — Pulkit Arya, Saurabh Bhaskar and Ankit Gupta — and sentenced them to life imprisonment.Murugesan said the state government had taken steps to ensure expeditious judicial proceedings and effective prosecution. He attributed the convictions to the evidence collected by the SIT and the arguments presented by the prosecution.All three convicts are currently in jail, serving their life sentences, he said.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. articles.title: Delhi high court declines to stop CJP’s Connaught Place protest, records police assurance on regulation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Thursday declined to pass an order restraining the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and its founder Abhijeet Dipke from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Thursday declined to pass an order restraining the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and its founder Abhijeet Dipke from holding a protest at Connaught Place on Friday, while taking on record Delhi Police’s assurance that all possible legal measures would be taken to regulate the gathering.The court was hearing a plea filed by Anil Kumar Gupta, a Palika Bazar street vendor, seeking to prevent protests in Connaught Place and other areas of central Delhi, citing concerns over traffic disruption, business losses and livelihood.Delhi Police told the court that it had taken steps to regulate the proposed protest and would take “all possible steps” in accordance with the law. The court recorded the assurance and posted the matter for November 3.The plea sought directions restraining CJP from holding any agitation, demonstration, march or gathering at Central Park in Connaught Place or at any other location that is not a designated protest venue.The matter was mentioned before a bench led by acting chief justice Nitin W Sambre by senior advocate Sacchin Puri, who sought immediate intervention, arguing that the protest could disrupt normal life, cause severe traffic bottlenecks and lead to financial losses for shop owners in central Delhi.Why CJP plans a Tricolour protestDipke has called on people to gather at Central Park in Connaught Place at 5pm on Friday with the national flag, following the arrest and remand of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.The two leaders were sent to five days of judicial custody after being arrested along with party activist Ajinkya Shinde for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar without authorisation. articles.title: Shraddha Dubey in Nepal? Police hunt intensifies as new CCTV footage emerges
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: The search for absconding Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the high-profile Shiva Sharma death case, has reportedly extended beyond India,
articles.body: LUCKNOW: The search for absconding Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the high-profile Shiva Sharma death case, has reportedly extended beyond India, with investigators following leads suggesting that she may be in Nepal. Photographs circulating on social media and CCTV footage purportedly showing Dubey with her sister Rashmi Dubey and an associate identified as Adil have provided fresh clues in a case that has gripped Lucknow over the past week.According to reports, the trio was last traced to Mahinagar in Nepal, where CCTV cameras allegedly captured them crossing a road and entering a local bus station. Sources said the three spent the night at the facility and boarded a bus the following morning, leaving before law enforcement teams could reach the location. While the footage has sparked speculation, police are yet to officially verify the identities of the individuals seen in the videos.The reported Nepal trail has added a new dimension to the investigation into the death of 28-year-old businessman and restaurateur Shiva Sharma, who died after falling from the fourth floor of an apartment building near Balu Adda in Hazratganj on October 9. Sharma’s family has alleged foul play and accused Shraddha and others of involvement in his death. She has consistently denied the allegations.Investigators believe the accused may have fled Lucknow shortly after the incident. A major lead emerged when Shraddha’s Scorpio SUV, bearing registration number UP 32 QQ 0111, was reportedly found parked at a private parking facility in Rupaidiha in Bahraich district on October 10, near the India-Nepal border. The discovery strengthened suspicions that the accused may have crossed into Nepal after abandoning the vehicle.Police teams have been working across multiple locations to trace Shraddha, Rashmi and the third accused. However, despite the emergence of CCTV footage and photographs, their exact whereabouts remain unknown. Officials are attempting to verify the visuals and reconstruct the group’s movements after they allegedly entered Nepal.Lucknow Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to Shraddha Dubey’s arrest. Similar rewards have also been announced for other accused in the case.Meanwhile, as police intensify efforts to track her down, Shraddha has continued to release video statements on social media defending herself against the allegations. In multiple videos posted over the past few days, she has claimed that Sharma died by suicide rather than murder. She has also appealed to the media and the public not to link her to politicians, bureaucrats or other influential personalities based on speculation and social media posts.In one of the videos, Shraddha alleged that Sharma was under severe financial stress and burdened with debts of ₹15 lakh to ₹20 lakh. According to her, he frequently received calls from creditors and had spoken about ending his life if he failed to repay the money. She has urged investigators to examine CCTV footage, mobile phone data and call detail records, claiming these would support her version of events. These claims have not been independently verified.Police say the circumstances leading to Sharma’s fall, the movements of the accused after the incident and evidence from multiple sources will be critical to the ongoing investigation. articles.title: Hollywood actress Pat Crowley’s Bel-Air home lists for nearly $16 million after more than 50 years; Howard Hughes once landed a plane nearby
articles.summary: A piece of Hollywood history has come to market in Bel-Air for the first time in more than fifty years.
articles.body: A piece of Hollywood history has come to market in Bel-Air for the first time in more than fifty years. The home of actress Pat Crowley, whose career stretched from Hollywood's Golden Age into television's glory days, sits at the eighth hole of the Bel-Air Country Club golf course and is listed for just under sixteen million dollars. It was the scene of dinner parties that mixed entertainment, sports and media royalty, and it offers ocean views, six bedrooms and seven bathrooms. This article explains what the property offers, who lived and entertained there, and stories that built its reputation.Inside 551 Perugia Way, nearly 6,000-square-foot Bel-Air home on the eighth hole of a golf courseThe residence at 551 Perugia Way covers nearly 6,000 square feet and counts six bedrooms and seven bathrooms, according to The Real Deal. It stands on a unique parcel at the eighth hole of the Bel-Air Country Club golf course, with unobstructed views of the course and, beyond it, the ocean. Its orientation also keeps it out of the path of any stray golf balls flying into the backyard. It is listed for just under $16 million, or $2,671 per square foot, and Drew Fenton, co-founder and chief executive officer of Carolwood Estates, holds the listing. The sale marks the first time the house has been on the market in more than fifty years, a milestone that gives buyers a rare chance to acquire a property long associated with Hollywood entertaining.Pat Crowley's Hollywood career, from a 1954 Golden Globes new star of the year title to television famePat Crowley built a career that spanned Hollywood's Golden Age and television's glory days. She was named new star of the year at the 1954 Golden Globes and made a name for herself during Hollywood's golden age with films such as Money from Home and Forever Female. She later went on to television, with roles including Joan Nash in Please Don't Eat the Daisies in 1965. Crowley passed away at the age of 91. For readers curious about the person behind the address, those credits describe an actress whose working life crossed two eras of American entertainment, moving from the big screen to the small screen. The Perugia Way house, bought in the early 1970s, became the setting for the entertaining that later defined her household.A family sanctuary since 1970s, how Pat Crowley and Ed Hookstratten bought the Bel-Air propertyCrowley purchased the home in the early 1970s with her then-husband, Ed Hookstratten, a prominent sports and entertainment attorney, according to the report. Their son, Jon Hookstratten, who is executive vice president of administration and operations at Sony Pictures Entertainment, grew up in the house along with his sister, Ann Hookstratten. Jon told The Real Deal that houses nearby have changed hands multiple times, yet his mother loved this one and never wanted to part with it. "It was her sanctuary," he said. After the purchase, the family enjoyed what Jon described as a high point of frequent dinner parties before his parents divorced. Those years, and the decision to keep the house for so long, give the listing a personal history beyond its architecture.Howard Hughes, Katharine Hepburn and a landing plane; Hollywood lore behind the Perugia Way houseLong before Crowley and her husband moved their family in, the property was already part of Hollywood lore, the report explains. Film producer and aviator Howard Hughes once landed his plane outside the back of the house to meet Katharine Hepburn, who happened to be playing golf at the time. The story fits the setting, the house sits on a unique parcel at the eighth hole of the Bel-Air Country Club golf course, with unobstructed views of the course and beyond to the ocean. For buyers who value a home's history as much as its square footage, the tale adds a layer of cinematic folklore to a property already distinguished by its location.Dinner parties with Johnny Carson, Fred Astaire and Muhammad Ali, guests who contributed to its fameCrowley and Ed Hookstratten's purchase was followed by frequent dinner parties where famous faces from entertainment, sports and media collided. Guests included Johnny Carson, Helen Hayes, Fred Astaire, Tom Brokaw and Tom Snyder. Jon remembered the mix as unusual, fun and full of very nice people, he told The Real Deal. He added that his mother loved to entertain and would host dinners for ten people, describing the gatherings as a Los Angeles cross section. One guest stood out among all, he said, recalling how while he lived in the guest house as a college student, doing homework, his mother nudged him to meet the visitors after he first waved off the invitation. In the main house, he found Muhammad Ali, and he still keeps the photograph he took with the heavyweight champion at his desk.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Washington flew 6,000 logs by helicopter into 24 miles of remote streams to rebuild salmon spawning grounds and help creeks hold water
articles.summary: Helicopters were used to place more than 6,000 logs into remote streams in central Washington as part of Northwest’s largest river restoration efforts.
articles.body: Helicopters were used to place more than 6,000 logs into remote streams in central Washington as part of Northwest’s largest river restoration efforts. The project focuses on remote waterways inaccessible by road and aims to restore habitats for salmon and bull trout. According to Northwest Public Broadcasting, the work covers more than 24 miles of streams across the Yakama Reservation and ceded lands. The logs create pools and sheltered areas for fish, while trapping gravel that fish use to spawn. They also reduce the speed of the current, allowing water to spread across floodplains, seep into the ground, and gradually return to streams.How are helicopters transporting thousands of logs to remote streamsThe project involves Yakama Nation habitat biologists and partner organizations, including The Nature Conservancy and Mid Columbia Fisheries Enhancement Group. At the time, fisheries specialists often viewed large log jams as barriers that prevented fish from moving freely.That approach has since changed, with the project returning more than 6,000 logs to waterways across Central Washington. Helicopters carried the timber from staging areas to sections of streams that roads no longer reach.Biologists use pink and blue flagging tape to show pilots where the logs should be placed. The project covers more than 24 miles of streams on tribal and other lands.Where do the logs come from, and how are they transported to remote streamsThe logs, which include Douglas fir, grand fir and cedar, come from forest-thinning work carried out by ‘The Nature Conservancy’. While some of the timber could have been sold, other logs would not have been sold. Reese Lolley, the organisation’s director of forest restoration and fire in Washington, said, “We’re thinking more towards whole landscape restoration, both the aquatic and the upland”.Removing selected trees can also help reduce the risk of large fires. Helicopters allow teams to transport timber from remote areas where building roads would be impractical or too expensive. The logs are then placed in streams to restore fish habitats and help reconnect waterways with surrounding floodplains.How do logs help restore fish habitats damaged by past river managementLogs make waterways more varied by creating sheltered spaces where salmon and bull trout can swim and spawn. They also form pools and trap gravel that fish need for spawning. Aquatic insects feed on algae growing on the wood.The restoration project aims to address damage caused by past practices, including overgrazing, railroad logging, splash dam logging, and the removal of wood from streams.Phil Rigdon, director of the Yakama Nation Department of Natural Resources, said, “We’re trying to learn from our mistakes and find a better way to manage.”How can the logs help streams retain water as the climate warmsThe logs slow the movement of water, allowing it to collect in pools and seep into the ground. They also help water spread across floodplains, where it can be stored and gradually released back into streams. This process helps keep waterways cooler and may reduce the risk of streams running dry.Kelly Clayton, a habitat biologist with the Yakama Nation, said, “This project is what will keep our creeks from running dry.”Nicolai said, “Back in the day, when they ran bulldozers down the creek, cleaning it out, making the water run off faster, that disconnected these floodplains from the river.”“We used to treat our streams like they were just for drainage - get the water off the land. articles.body: A missile heading towards the Saudi Arabia's Medina region was intercepted and destroyed, Saudi led coalition, which is on war with Houthis in Yemen, claimed on Thursday.Coalition spokesperson major general Turki al-Maliki announced the interception on the social media platform X."Coalition: Interception and destruction of a cruise missile in the Medina region," Maliki wrote.No further information was shared regarding who launched the missile or its intended targetMeanwhile, Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree has clarified that no strikes were launched towards the Medina region, nullifying the Saudi claims."The Yemeni Armed Forces confirm that they did not carry out today any targeting operation directed toward Saudi territories," Saree wrote on X."What the Saudi enemy claims regarding targeting toward the city of Medina is a great and immense falsehood," he added.The remarks come amid intense exchange of airstrikes between Houthis and coalition forces, with each targeting other's airport infrastructure.According to Turkish news agency Anadolu, Thursday’s incident came hours after the coalition claimed intercepting and destroying a drone over Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province.Previously Saudi Arabia accused the Iran-aligned group of targeting the cities of Mecca and Medina, which are considered sacred by the Muslims.Houthis, on the other hand, had exempted the regions from strikes, while claiming every other air infrastructure to be on their radar.On Wednesday, the coalition announced that it had destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards the Saudi capital Riyadh.Saudi Arabia leads a military coalition supporting Yemen’s government against the Houthis since 2015.
